corrections.why: NHLR and HistoriCorps both give a 60-foot tower (about 18.3 m). 24.4 m is 80 feet, the height in a 2000 news report quoted by Forest Lookouts.
HistoriCorps scheduled 2024 volunteer sessions to finish the cabin. No source read confirms the work was completed.
HistoriCorps says volunteers worked on restoring the cabin. It does not say the restoration was completed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1936, and a 1936 Mountain Democrat notice planned the tower that year. HistoriCorps gives 1937. The story reports both dates.
NHLR and HistoriCorps give 60 feet. A 2000 news report quoted by Forest Lookouts gives 80 feet. The story uses 60 feet and notes the 80-foot figure.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 24.4 is 80 feet; corrected to 18.3 m (60 feet) per NHLR and HistoriCorps. Elevation differs: NHLR 6,192 ft, HistoriCorps and Campflare 6,225 ft; not in facts or story. The closed-to-public status rests on an undated third-party Campflare listing that cites no Forest Service page; check the Eldorado National Forest before relying on it. The Eldorado cabins page grep found no Alder Ridge mention. A 2000 news item on the Forest Lookouts page reports a death at the lookout; it is left out of the story as not needed for the history. No source read gives staffing or fire history, and no source confirms a rental has opened. No photos added.
